claims.text: Refractory Group IV HEAs processed from hydride precursors require a two-stage thermal history.
Vacuum heating at 500–600 K decomposes TiH2 or ZrH2 and releases hydrogen.
Keeping hydride decomposition below 600 K prevents oxygen uptake by avoiding a high-temperature oxidation window.
Hot extrusion at 1400–1500 K under vacuum below 10^-6 Pa will densify the Group IV HEA powder.
Either vacuum below 10^-6 Pa or inert gas containing less than 1 ppm O2 is sufficient to control oxygen during processing.
A 30-minute hold near 600 K, rapid heating to 1450 K, and extrusion at 50–80 MPa constitute a suitable processing schedule.
Increasing the SPS temperature of CrMoNbWV from 1200 °C to 1400 °C decreases the Laves-phase fraction through reverse dissolution and enhanced diffusion.
The CrMoNbWV result implies that extrusion above 1400 K will dissolve brittle Laves phases in Group IV HEAs.
High-temperature processing causes grain growth or grain coarsening.
High-temperature diffusion and grain coarsening suppress oxygen-induced alpha-HCP precipitation in Group IV HEAs.
HIP-processed equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can contain an NbTaTi-rich BCC phase and a ZrHf-rich HCP phase.
The HCP phase in Group IV HEAs is precipitated by oxygen uptake and is responsible for embrittlement.
Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries promote cracking and low plasticity.
Reducing the fraction of grain-boundary brittle phases in Group IV HEAs will reduce catastrophic cracking.
The proposed extrusion route will produce a dense bulk form with less than 1% residual porosity.
The proposed route will significantly reduce the Laves-phase fraction.
The proposed route will significantly reduce the alpha-HCP phase fraction.
Controlled retention of metastable precipitates will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Grain refinement produced by the proposed route will contribute to enhanced high-temperature yield strength.
Conventional high-temperature processing in air or low vacuum produces oxygen contents above 1 wt%, extensive alpha-HCP precipitation, and catastrophic cracking.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism predict grain growth or coarsening during high-temperature extrusion, whereas the predicted outcome attributes strengthening to grain refinement.
